Judge: A wins all four pairs decisively, and none is close. Every A frame has AAA character fidelity (skin pores, scars, tattoos, fabric weave, stitching, engraved weapons). Its materials are physically convincing: chrome, glossy paint, weathered stucco, chain link, individual grass blades, snow. Each A frame is composed around a clear hero focal subject and carries narrative life (fire, pursuit, fleeing pedestrians, stained-glass night mood). The B frames share a coherent warm golden-hour look, decent atmospheric haze and a recognisable Singapore setting (shophouses, hawker centre, landmark towers, supertrees). But they read as a prototype. Characters are smooth and doll-like. Oversized bloom muzzle flashes swallow hands and weapons, and the shooter looks at the camera rather than down the sights. Streets and the hawker centre are nearly empty, with very little traffic and rigid NPC clumps. There are placeholder and debug elements: a blank green sign, a grid-only minimap, duplicated 'You lost the search.' text that contradicts 'SEARCHING 0s', and a stray red arc in the sky. A malformed tube-and-ring prop sits at the centre of one frame, HUD covers the player character, and framing has no strong focal point. Fixes in order of impact for B: (1) close-range hero and weapon fidelity, with a correct aim pose and gaze along the sights; (2) muzzle flash shrunk to a compact burst; (3) crowd and traffic density in streets and the hawker centre; (4) remove debug overlays and placeholder or malformed props; (5) camera framing so the armed hero is readable and not under the minimap.
